cards.front: Recall a key point about Contemporary Latin Music
cards.back: Clave is a two-bar rhythmic pattern (3-2 or 2-3) that underpins virtually all Latin music — all other rhythmic parts align with the clave.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contemporary Latin Music
cards.back: Bossa nova is a Brazilian style blending samba rhythms with jazz harmonies — gentle, syncopated guitar patterns and soft vocal delivery.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contemporary Latin Music
cards.back: Salsa features piano montuno (repeated syncopated pattern), brass riffs, and layered percussion — it creates high-energy dance music through rhythmic complexity.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Contemporary Latin Music
cards.back: Tango and habanera share the distinctive rhythmic pattern (dotted quaver-semiquaver-quaver-quaver) — tango added dramatic expression and bandoneón.

cards.front: What should you know about music exam tips?
cards.back: Identify clave pattern (3-2 or 2-3). Name genre-specific rhythms (bossa nova, samba, tango, habanera). Identify percussion instruments. Explain syncopation and off-beat patterns.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Latin music is just dance music with a fast beat. Correct: Latin music has specific, identifiable rhythmic patterns: clave (3-2 or 2-3), bossa nova pattern, samba rhythm, tango/habanera rhythm. Each genre has distinct instrumentation, texture and vocal styles. The exam expects you to name these features using precise AQA terminology.
Identify the clave pattern and explain how it organises the rhythm in a Latin music track. Name at least three other Latin rhythmic features from the AQA list.

cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: Contemporary Latin Music
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Show knowledge of Contemporary Latin Music using appropriate musical vocabulary (e.g. terminology for elements, devices, and contexts).

Contemporary Latin Music is a key element of GCSE Music requiring theoretical understanding and practical application. The AQA specification requires you to identify, describe and analyse this element in set works and unfamiliar music. cards.front: Applying Contemporary Latin Music in Performance and Composition
cards.back: Understanding contemporary latin music informs your performing (AO1) and composing (AO2) work. In performance, awareness of contemporary latin music helps you make interpretive decisions that serve the music. In composition, contemporary latin music provides the building blocks of your creative work — the choices you make about this element shape the identity and coherence of your piece.

cards.front: Exam Technique for Contemporary Latin Music Questions
cards.back: In the AQA GCSE Music listening exam, questions about contemporary latin music typically ask you to: identify features by ear; describe how they are used; explain their effect; compare features between extracts. The key to success is precise terminology — never use vague language.
